lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Hey Marcus. How's it going? You look like you've been in the query planner for three days straight.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, is it that obvious? Yeah, I'm good. Tired, but good. The funnel stuff finally clicked on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I saw. Two point eight seconds down to under a second. That's great work. I shared it in the leadership channel.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Oh, thanks. I didn't know that.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yeah, Dana replied with three fire emojis, which for Dana is basically a standing ovation.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, I'll take it.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So I have a couple of things I want to cover. Some feedback, and I want to talk about the staff engineer conversation we started last month. But first, anything on your mind? This is your time.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Yeah, actually, a couple of things. One is small. The on call rotation. I've been on it every third week for about eight months now and it's starting to wear on me a bit.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay. Tell me more. Is it the frequency or the pages themselves?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Mostly the pages. Like, I got woken up four times last rotation, and three of them were the same flaky disk alert on the old ingestion box. Nobody owns it, so it just keeps firing.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Ugh, yeah. That's not okay. That's a broken alert, not an on call problem.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Right. And I don't want to complain, but--

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: You're not complaining, this is exactly the kind of thing I want to hear. Two things. Nina joins the rotation next week, so you go from every third week to every fourth. And I'll ask Kevin to either fix or delete that disk alert by end of next week.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: That would help a lot. Honestly just the disk alert would be most of it.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay, I'm writing that down. Kevin, disk alert, by October second. What's the second thing?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The second thing is bigger. It's about the AI Insights project. I keep hearing it's going to be the big Q4 bet, and I'm a bit worried about how it's being scoped.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay. Worried how?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So from what I've seen in the doc, the plan is to run an LLM over every customer's event stream every night and generate insights. But nobody's done the math on cost. For Globex alone that's something like four hundred million events a month.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yeah. That's a fair concern. I've heard the same thing from Arjun.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: And I think there's a smarter version where you precompute anomalies with plain statistics, and only send the interesting slices to the model. Like, ninety nine percent cheaper.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Have you written that down anywhere?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Not really. Just in my head and a couple of Slack threads.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay, so that's actually a nice segue into the feedback I wanted to give you. Can I share it now?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Yeah, go for it.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So the positive first, and I mean this. Your technical judgment is excellent. The funnel work, the way you debugged the rebalancing issue in July, people trust your calls. When Marcus says something is a bad idea, people listen.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Thanks. That's nice to hear.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: The growth area is that a lot of that judgment stays in Slack threads and hallway conversations. Like what you just told me about AI Insights. That's a really important idea, and right now it lives in your head. If it's not written down, it doesn't influence the roadmap.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Yeah. That's, yeah. That's fair. I kind of hate writing docs. It feels slow.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I know. And I'm not asking for a forty page design doc. But at the staff level, the job is less about writing the best code and more about making sure the org makes the right technical decisions. And that happens in writing.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay. So for the AI Insights thing, what would you want to see?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: A two page doc. What's the proposed approach, what's your approach, rough cost comparison, and the risks. If you can get that to me by Wednesday the first, I'll make sure it's pre-read for Q4 planning on Thursday.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Wednesday is tight, but doable. Can Hannah review it? She knows the model cost side way better than I do.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yes, great idea. Loop her in. And honestly, that's another staff behavior, pulling in the right people.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, look at me, being staff already.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Ha, one doc at a time. Okay, so that leads into the career conversation. Last month you said you wanted to go for staff engineer in the next cycle. Is that still true?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Yeah, definitely. I've been thinking about it a lot. I think I want it, but I also want to make sure I'm not just chasing a title.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's a good instinct. What do you think it would mean for your day to day?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I guess less feature work, more cross team stuff. Setting technical direction. Maybe mentoring Nina and Aman more formally.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yeah, that's about right. And for what it's worth, you already mentor Aman informally. He told me your code reviews are the most useful ones he gets.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Oh really? I always feel like I'm being too picky.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: He said picky but kind. Which is the best combination.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay, I'll put that on my tombstone. Picky but kind.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Ha. So here's how I'd frame the gap. Our staff rubric has four areas: technical depth, scope of impact, written communication, and developing others. You're clearly at staff level on technical depth. Developing others, you're close. Scope and writing are where I need to see more evidence.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay. What does evidence look like for scope?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Owning something that spans more than one team. For example, the query engine migration. If you led that, deleting the old engine, coordinating with platform and the frontend team, that's a staff sized project.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Oh, I would love to kill the old query engine. I've been wanting to do that for a year.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I know, you mention it about once a week.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, guilty.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: So here's what I'm proposing. You write the AI Insights cost doc by Wednesday. Then, assuming it gets prioritized at planning, you lead the query engine migration in Q4, as the technical lead, including writing the design doc and running the weekly sync.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay. And the promo timeline?

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Promo packets are due in mid January. If the migration is on track and you've got two or three solid docs under your belt by then, I'd feel really good about putting you up. I can't promise the committee outcome, but I'd advocate hard.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: That's fair. I appreciate you being clear about it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Can I ask something about the migration? If I'm leading it, who's actually doing the work? Because if it's just me, it's three weeks minimum, and I'd also be doing the cohorts rewrite.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Good question. I was thinking you plus Aman, with Nina for the frontend switchover at the end. And the cohorts rewrite would move to Aman after the webhook work, so you're not doing both.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay, that's much more realistic. Aman's ready for it, honestly. He's been asking for something meatier.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: See, that's a staff sentence. You're thinking about Aman's growth, not just the project.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, stop, you're going to make me self conscious about every sentence now.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Ha, sorry. But one thing to watch. Leading means you'll write less code. Some people really struggle with that. How do you feel about it?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Honestly, a bit nervous. Writing code is how I know I had a productive day. If I spend a day in meetings and docs, it feels like I did nothing.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's super normal. One trick that helped me, write down at the end of each day what decisions got unblocked because of you. It's a different scoreboard. Try it for two weeks and tell me how it feels.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay, I'll try it. Decision journal. Very fancy.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: One more piece of feedback, a smaller one. In the architecture review two weeks ago, when Tom pushed back on the caching approach, you kind of went quiet and then did it your way anyway.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Yeah. I noticed that too, after. I didn't really want to argue with the Head of Product in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: I get it. But it ended up confusing people, because Tom thought we'd agreed to his approach. It's totally okay to disagree in the room. Tom actually likes it. He respects people who push back with data.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Okay. So next time, say it in the room. Or follow up in writing if it's not the right moment.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Exactly. Disagree and then commit, or disagree and then write it down. Either is fine. The quiet version isn't.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Got it. That's useful. Honestly I didn't realize it had that effect.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's why I'm telling you. It's not a big deal, it was a one off. Anything you want from me? Feedback goes both ways.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Hmm. Maybe one thing. Sometimes priorities change mid sprint and I find out in standup instead of before. Like the sharing bug last week. It'd be nice to get a heads up.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: That's fair. That one came from Siobhan late on Friday and I just dropped it in standup. I'll try to message the person directly before standup when something shifts. Call me out if I don't.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Will do. Politely.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Picky but kind.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, exactly.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Okay, let me recap. I'll make sure Kevin fixes or deletes the flaky disk alert by October second, and Nina joins on call next week. You'll write the two page AI Insights cost doc with Hannah's review by Wednesday the first. If prioritized, you'll lead the query engine migration in Q4. And we'll check in on the promo packet in early December.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Sounds good. And you'll ping me before standup when priorities shift.

lines.speaker: priya
lines.text: Yes. Deal. Thanks Marcus. Go get some sleep.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Ha, after one more query. Thanks Priya.
